V0ldek opened PR #14967 from V0ldek:v0ldek/amd-mpk to bytecodealliance:main:

While poking around in the pooling allocator I noticed that my machine actually does not use the MPK features, which was weird since I've used them before. Turns out AMD is just rejected by wasmtime for this feature. After looking into it I actually found a more critical issue.

The check for mpk::is_supported explicitly checked for GenuineIntel, and then for the PKU bit on the cpuid message. This is misguided for two reasons:

  1. Zen3 AMD also supports MPKs but wasmtime misses out on using them;
  2. the OSPKE bit also has to be checked to actually be correct.

Number 1. seems to have been done as an attempt to avoid CI crashes. In #7445, #7446 MPK was disabled and then reenabled for Intel only in PR #7513. I believe that was actually a red herring and those crashes were caused by the second point.

PKU only says if the CPU supports MPKs on the hardware level. However, the OS still needs to enable it (CR4.PKE). If it is not enabled, RDPKRU/WRPKRU raise #UD, which kills the process with SIGILL. An example is a VM that runs on a modern CPU as the hardware, but whose hypervisor has PKU disabled. This would actually fault on any vendor, Intel included. You can test it today on the old version by running wasmtime in QEMU with nopku passed (-append "nopku"), it will crash with the pooling allocator when it tries to set up PKs.

In this commit we switch to checking both PKE and OSPKE, removing the vendor check. This is confirmed to work on modern AMD and Intel, and correctly recognises MPK when ran under QEMU:

  • with -cpu host and default kernel settings (supported),
  • with -cpu host but nopku in the kernel (unsupported),
  • with -cpu host,-pku (unsupported).

We now have a test in tests/mpk.rs to ensure the result of the check agrees with actual capabilities the process has.

Additionally, removed a stale test in pkru::tests::check_read, it was ignored since forever and the new mpk test supersedes it.

If you want confirmation on the CPU bits to be read:

  • Intel SDM Volume 1, Chapter 21, Section 21.3, Table 21-20 (PDF at https://cdrdv2.intel.com/v1/dl/getContent/671436).
  • AMD64 Architecture Programmer's Manual, Volume 3, Appendix E, section E.3.6 (PDF at https://docs.amd.com/api/khub/documents/BqEoC2FadIAgbrUdEzDJIg/content).

:speech_balloon: V0ldek created PR review comment:

I'll need to work more on this and test how it interacts with different platforms. One finding is that I'm pretty sure we actually don't want to gate is_support behind x86_64 cause on 32-bit you can also use MPKs.

Another one is FreeBSD. They don't have libc pkey_alloc or pkey_free but they do support PKUs, so the is_support flag would actually say yes. Their API is different, so wasmtime would have to have a separate cfg path for FreeBSD: https://man.freebsd.org/cgi/man.cgi?query=pkru&sektion=3.

I have no idea what happens on macOS and no means to test it either.
V0ldek updated PR #14967.
github-actions[bot] added the label wasmtime:api on PR #14967.
:memo: V0ldek submitted PR review.

:speech_balloon: V0ldek created PR review comment:

So ARM also has its own MPK system, but it is different, e.g. they only have 7 usable keys instead of 15. It would also require rewriting the code in vm/mpk/pkru.rs.

At this point I honestly think that the test should just be "do we return false on those platforms", because FreeBSD and Linux on ARM support MPK architecturally, but wasmtime does not hook into that and it'd be a separate PR to allow that. I will try to figure out how hard it'd be for FreeBSD in this PR, but for ARM I have no machine to test it on so I wouldn't tackle that.
